end.summary:
Identified 3×3 as a square number and 3×4 as a rectangle.
Extended growing-row patterns: fourth row has 4 dots; five rows total 15 dots; next row has 7 dots and total 28.
Used the shared-corner idea when adding a row and column, giving 13 and 7 in two examples.
In the final overlap example, gave 19 and then 17; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Ishita practised reading picture patterns, adding successive rows, and distinguishing squares from rectangles using equal rows and columns. They explained that a shared corner must not be counted twice, and used this method correctly in earlier examples. In the last example, they gave two different totals (19 and then 17), so that calculation was not corrected before the lesson ended. At home, draw a small grid-growth example and ask Ishita to mark the shared corner before adding the new row and column.
